# What the data-dict export loses: Fatality Analysis Reporting System

The YAML files here follow data-dict spec 0.1.0. They describe the common data format, so they validate against its parquet files. The records in `metadata/` remain canonical. This table counts what the export drops or flattens into text.

| | `2024` | `2017` |
|---|---|---|
| variables exported | 40 | 40 |
| variables whose numeric code labels went to `details` (no labeled numeric codes) | 24 | 24 |
| missing or unresolved codes, typed only in the `__code` column's labels | 62 | 63 |
| availability entries (wave by form, with n), summarized as one line of text | 40 | 40 |
| field origins (publisher, data file, rule, hand, model) not exported | 286 | 286 |
| table references whose `when` condition is only in a description, and whose columns aren't marked foreign_key | 2 | 2 |
| links between releases, not exported | 40 | 40 |
| derived properties (scale signatures), not exported | 2 | 2 |
| code histories, not exported | 42 | 42 |
| release id not expressible as data-dict `version` (needs semver or a date) | 1 | 1 |
